lesson_body:
Welcome to Day 2 of our exciting Unit 2: Shapes and Spaces! Yesterday, we began our exploration into the wonderful world of shapes, learning to identify basic shapes such as circles, squares, triangles, and rectangles. Today, we will dive deeper into the characteristics of these shapes and how they fit into the spaces around us. 

To start, we will review the shapes we learned about yesterday by playing a game called 'Shape Hunt.' Each student will look around the classroom to find objects that match the shapes we learned about. For example, do you see something that is shaped like a circle? How about a square? As you find objects, we will gather together and share what we found, reinforcing our understanding of the shapes in our environment.

Next, we will introduce two new concepts: the number of sides and corners in each shape. Squares have four sides and four corners, while triangles have three sides and three corners. We will use colorful shape cut-outs to physically count and connect the number of sides to the shapes. Each child will pick a shape, and together we will trace it on the board, labeling the sides and corners as we go. This visual representation will help reinforce the lesson, making it more memorable.

Finally, we will conclude our lesson with a creativity session. Using different art supplies, each student will create their own shape collage on a piece of paper. They will select a variety of shapes, cut them out, and glue them onto their collage, discussing with peers how many sides and corners each shape has. This hands-on activity will allow students to express their understanding of shapes in an artistic way while cementing their learning through creativity.
interactive_assignment: For your interactive assignment, we will embark on a "Shape Scavenger Hunt" in our schoolyard or classroom. You will be divided into small groups. Each group will be given a checklist of shapes, including circles, squares, triangles, and rectangles. Your task is to find as many objects as possible that match the shapes on your checklist. Once you locate an object, you need to draw it on the back of your checklist and label the shape. After returning to the classroom, you'll present your findings to your classmates, sharing not only the objects you found but also how many sides and corners each one has. This activity will help you apply your knowledge in a fun and engaging setting!

daily_assessment.question: What shape has three sides and three corners?
